Social Welfare Functions

This scene merges two people's happiness into one score. It picks the best among all possible happiness pairs.

One slider changes how the merging works. Count only the sum, and the bigger total wins. Hate inequality more, and the score changes. At the extreme, only the worse-off person counts. The best point slides toward the equal diagonal. The formula below fixes the merging rule.

For example, two 🧑 friends split 15 🍬 candies. One friend gets 9 and the other gets 6. Judged by the sum alone, this split scores best. Care more about fairness, and they split 7.5 each. The worse-off friend's happiness sets the score.

Wρ=(u1ρ+u2ρ2)1/ρW_\rho = \left(\frac{u_1^\rho + u_2^\rho}{2}\right)^{1/\rho}Wρ​=(2u1ρ​+u2ρ​​)1/ρ
